title: Richardson Magazine, A12
abstract:
This issue explores California as both a myth and a mirror, an unreal place where cultural revolutions, personal reinventions, and private excess collide. Drawing from the voices of those who have lived its contradictions, the project examines California as a landscape of freedom and fantasy where creative possibility coexists with self-destruction. Through image and narrative, the issue traces the tension between the state’s iconic allure and the fragile realities behind it, revealing a world built on dreams, risk, and the constant sense that everything, good or bad, could vanish at any moment.

The project was led by art director Daniel Sansavini, with my collaboration as design assistant, contributing to 
the layout of magazine A12.
